spn_wl_brood.description:
Corvane. Webhunter, which is a trade about four people have ever practised and three of them stopped.

I've been inside the mouth of the Widow's Lair. Not far in - far enough to count, and counting is the job.

Hatchlings in the thousands.

I've said that figure out loud to three different officers and watched all three decide I was exaggerating. I was not. I counted a section and multiplied, which is how anybody counts anything that doesn't hold still.

And silk-bound weavers tending them, which is the part that should worry people more than the number.

Something in there is being looked after.

Thin the first rooms before anyone tries the deeper ones. That's the whole of this job and I'd not pretend it's more.

Hatchlings first. The weavers sit above them and spit, and you will not see the first one.
spn_wl_brood.accept_text: Inside the Lair, around the Web Heart.
spn_wl_brood.turn_in_text:
Fewer legs.

That's the best thing I can say about that place right now and I've been trying to think of a second one for a week.

Take this.

spn_wl_silka.description:
The hive buds off a single queen and her name is Silka.

West lair, off the Web Heart.

Here's what that means, and it's the reason I'm sending you at her rather than at the numbers.

Everything Longleg ever was came out of her eggs. Every spider in those woods that anybody has ever lost a dog or a child to - that's one line, from one source, and the source is still laying.

I'd assumed for years that the woods simply had spiders. Woods do.

Then I counted, and the count only works if there's one.

End the line.

Follow the egg sacs west. They get thicker the closer you are, which I'd call helpful if it were anything else.

She's what they're all running from. I don't have a better way to put it and I've watched them do it.
spn_wl_silka.accept_text: The west lair, off the Web Heart. Follow the egg sacs.
spn_wl_silka.turn_in_text:
No more eggs.

For the first time since the plague, these woods will have fewer legs in them next year than this one.

Thank you. I've waited a long while to be able to say a sentence like that.

spn_wl_skitter.description:
There's a second queen-brood in the east lair, under a weaver called Skitter.

And she is not Silka with a different name. I want that clear before you go in with the same plan.

Silka lays. That's all she does - she's a source, and the hive flows away from her.

Skitter keeps.

She hangs her victims from the ceiling for later. Alive, some of them, for considerably longer than you'd think possible, and I have been close enough to the mouth of that lair to establish that and I wish I hadn't.

I've watched it from the mouth for a season.

I would like to stop watching it. That's the honest whole of my reason and it isn't strategic.

East of the Web Heart.

And look up before you step in. Not after. Before.
spn_wl_skitter.accept_text: The east lair, off the Web Heart. Look up before you step in.
spn_wl_skitter.turn_in_text:
Hung up like laundry. The whole east lair.

Well.

Not any more.

spn_wl_venom.description:
Apothecary Pell. Don't lean over the cauldron, it's at a delicate stage and so am I.

My venom theory has acquired a new requirement, which is what theories do when they're going well.

I need stalker venom.

The Silverpine spider glands I've been working with are adequate and they are not strong enough - by a good half, which I established the tedious way over four months and eleven batches.

The Venom Stalkers inside the Lair have what I want.

Cut the sac at the base. Seal it. Then run, and I'd like those three verbs kept in that order because two of my suppliers reversed the last two.

And please don't open one to look.

Everybody wants to look. It's green, it's famous, and the one who looked is why I now say this to everybody.
spn_wl_venom.accept_text: Off the venom stalkers inside the Widow's Lair. Seal them.
spn_wl_venom.turn_in_text:
Oh, that is beautiful. Thick as syrup, green as a corpse.

The Dark Lady's Apothecaries will want to hear about this, and for once I'll be the one telling them.

spn_wl_larder.description:
Now the job I've been putting off, and I'd rather tell you why than dress it up as reconnaissance.

I want to know how many people that hive has eaten.

Not approximately. The number.

Because I've spent nine years telling families in these woods that their people were lost to wolves, or to the road, or to the pines - and I believed most of it when I said it, and the ones I didn't believe I said anyway.

The answer's in two places, deep in.

The Larder, far west of the Web Heart, where they hang the fresh ones.

And the Husk Pit, far east, where they drop what's left.

Stand in each one long enough to count.

That's all I'm asking. Don't bring anything out. I don't want anything brought out.
spn_wl_larder.accept_text: The Larder far west of the Web Heart, and the Husk Pit far east.
spn_wl_larder.turn_in_text:
Forty-one. And you stopped counting.

Thank you.

I'll write to a few families who are going to hate me for it, and they'll be right to.

spn_wl_journal.description:
[A silk-wrapped page, pulled off a Brood Warden's carapace. It has been in there a while.]

It's a hunter's hand. Small, cramped, written fast - the hand of somebody writing in a bad light who expected to be reading it back later.

The last entry begins:

'I have counted the exits, and there are only two.'

There is nothing after that line. Not a torn edge - the page simply stops, and the rest of it is blank, and the ink on the last word is heavier than the rest as though the pen stayed where it was for a while.

The silk around it was spun afterward. Deliberately, and tightly, the way the weavers wrap anything they intend to keep.

[The Apothecary at the Rear Guard keeps a list of the missing. He has kept it for eleven years and he keeps it properly.]
spn_wl_journal.accept_text: Take it to Apothecary Pell at the Rear Guard, with the cauldron.
spn_wl_journal.turn_in_text:
Marek Dunn.

I had him down as lost to wolves. I've had him down as that for two years and I wrote it myself.

A spider is worse. And better - he was somebody doing his job, right up to the last line of it.

I'll correct the list.

spn_wl_velaxis.description:
Above the Web Heart there's a spire, and Velaxis nests in it.

Older than Silka. Larger than Skitter. And not fond of company, which in anything else I'd call a personality and in her I'd call a warning.

She is the head of this hive.

Not the source - Silka was that. Not the keeper - that was Skitter. The head, meaning that both of those answered upward, and I did not believe spiders did that until I spent a season at the mouth of that place watching them.

Cut it off and the hive is a lot of legs with nothing arranging them.

Up the north neck from the Web Heart.

The Spire is lit by her eyes. That's not a figure of speech, it's how you'll know you've arrived, and it's the last useful thing I can tell you.

I'm not going to pretend this is anything but a death sentence for whoever tries it. I've watched two go up that neck.
spn_wl_velaxis.accept_text: Up the north neck from the Web Heart, into the Matriarch's Spire.
spn_wl_velaxis.turn_in_text:
Eight eyes, all closed.

I'll rest easy tonight, and so will these woods, and I have not written that word in a report in eleven years.

You've earned every copper and a good deal more I haven't got.

sps_at_vestibule.description:
Magister Orsolo. With Quillfire silent I can finally say this out loud without somebody shouting it down.

That waygate was keeping something.

Everybody has treated it as a door nobody uses. A door nobody uses is a door that has been left - this one has been MAINTAINED, and the difference is visible from the outside if you know what a maintained ward looks like.

So something on the other side was worth the upkeep, and somebody was paying it until very recently.

The tower's lowest rooms are a vestibule and a reading hall above it.

Stand in both and tell me whether the lamps are still lit.

That's the entire ask and I know it sounds trivial. It isn't. Those lamps don't burn oil. If they're lit, something is still putting power into that building, and if they're violet, it is listening.
sps_at_vestibule.accept_text: Step into the waygate - the vestibule first, then the reading hall up the stair.
sps_at_vestibule.turn_in_text:
Still lit. Violet.

So it's listening.

Thank you. Truly - I've been arguing for permission to ask that question for two years.

sps_at_mages.description:
The reading hall is staffed by the dead, and I use the word staffed deliberately.

Kirin Tor and Forsaken mages who kept studying after they stopped breathing.

That's not a haunting. A haunting repeats. These are working - moving between lecterns, taking things down, putting things back, and the thing that finally convinced me was that the stacks are in order.

Somebody is shelving.

And there are imps bound to the lecterns, which tells you the binding was done by a living hand at some point, because an imp does not stay on a lectern out of professional interest.

I want the hall cleared so a scribe can walk it.

The mages cast first - all of them, immediately, and they do not posture about it.

The imps hold the doors. Expect to fight your way back out as well as in.
sps_at_mages.accept_text: The Reading Hall and the galleries above it.
sps_at_mages.turn_in_text:
A scribe can walk it now.

Perhaps even a very brave librarian, and I know two.

sps_at_tomes.description:
Tome wraiths are the pages of a book that learned to hover.

I'd like to be less flippant and I've tried three other descriptions and that one is the most accurate.

They haunt the galleries. And they are all from the same book, which nobody has noticed because nobody has held two of them side by side.

I have a theory about who wrote it.

I'm not going to tell you the theory before you go, and I'd ask you to let me have that - because if I name him now and I'm wrong, I'll spend the rest of my life having named him.

Torn pages, off the wraiths in the galleries.

Enough that I can set them out together, because a single page is a hand and a stack is a hand I can be certain of.

And do not read aloud. Not a syllable, not to yourself, not to see what happens. That is the one instruction I'd actually enforce.
sps_at_tomes.accept_text: Off the tome wraiths in the tower's galleries. Don't read aloud.
sps_at_tomes.turn_in_text:
I know this hand.

Hawren. It was Hawren all along.

Hawren, who taught me to read.

sps_at_hawren.description:
[Orsolo is a long time getting to it, and when he does he is very matter-of-fact.]

Magister Hawren keeps the Archivist's Gallery.

He was my teacher. I've told you that already and I'll say it once more properly, because the next part doesn't make sense without it: he taught me to read, and then to read carefully, and then that the second one is a different skill.

He no longer remembers a pupil's name.

I know that for a fact. I stood in the vestibule eleven days ago and said my own name up that stair, twice, and the gallery did not change.

So there's nothing to be recovered and I've stopped looking for a version where there is.

The Archivist's Gallery, west of the reading hall. He's surrounded by his own pages.

I cannot do it myself.

I'd like that on the record as cowardice rather than protocol, because that's what it is.
sps_at_hawren.accept_text: The Archivist's Gallery, west of the reading hall.
sps_at_hawren.turn_in_text:
He'd want to be remembered for something better.

I'll try to oblige. I've all his pages now, and that's more of him than most teachers leave.

sps_at_spellblades.description:
Haskell. Millwright - or I was, when there was a mill worth the title.

Our saws were enchanted to run themselves. That was the whole innovation and it was mine, and I was proud of it for about nine years.

The blades in that tower are the same kind of fool.

Bright, quick, and completely indifferent to who they cut. That's not malice - a saw has no malice. It's that somebody built a thing to keep going and never built the half that decides when not to.

I know exactly how that happens. I did it to a sawmill.

I've lost two apprentices to the lesser ones in that tower.

Two. Both of them in there on my say-so, looking at blades because I wanted to know whether the enchantment was the same as ours.

It is the same as ours.

All through the tower. They're the ones that glint, and they don't tire, and neither does the thing that made them.
sps_at_spellblades.accept_text: Throughout the tower. They're the ones that glint.
sps_at_spellblades.turn_in_text:
Quieter.

I've got my last two apprentices counting sawblades and sorting nails, and that is all I will be asking of them for a month.

Possibly longer.

sps_at_reagents.description:
The Alchemy Lab was Dalaran's best-stocked apothecary outside the Violet Citadel.

I want that understood as a quantity, not a compliment. That is an enormous amount of material in one room, catalogued, sealed, and sitting there.

And its alchemists never stopped brewing.

Decades of that. In a sealed room. With no one taking anything out.

I'm a millwright and even I can see where that ends - every batch they finish has to go somewhere, and it's been going into the floor, and the floor is above the lower hall.

I want sealed vials out of there before the slow poison gets properly out of hand.

Not all of it. I know I can't have all of it.

Enough that somebody who understands this better than me can say what's in the floor.

The Forsaken Alchemists carry them on their belts. North-east of the lower hall. Follow the smell, and don't breathe it.
sps_at_reagents.accept_text: The Alchemy Lab, north-east of the lower hall.
sps_at_reagents.turn_in_text:
Sealed, thank the Light, and not yet leaking.

I'll have them neutralised by dawn and I'll not sleep until they are.

sps_at_ledger.description:
[A ledger, pulled out of an alchemist's coat. The cover is stained through with something that was once a flask.]

It's kept properly. Ruled lines, dated columns, a running total at the foot of each page - the work of somebody who was never going to be audited and did it correctly anyway.

And it is page after page of orders for 'reagents of discretion'.

That exact phrase, every time, for years. Never a description, never a quantity in plain words, never a name for what was actually in the crate.

Every single order is initialled.

The same two letters, in the same careful hand, down the whole right-hand margin of every page.

H.

[The millwright at the mill has been buying from the same valley his whole working life. He'll know the initials, and he'll know them immediately.]
sps_at_ledger.accept_text: Take it to Haskell at the mill. He'll recognise the initials.
sps_at_ledger.turn_in_text:
H.

Helbrim.

He sold the mill its lamp-oil for eleven years. Came by in person. Asked after my apprentices by name.

I'd have said he was a decent man and I'd have said it in front of anybody.

Not any more.

sps_at_helbrim.description:
Apothecary Helbrim runs that lab.

If running is the word for a man who has been brewing the same batch for decades, and I've decided it isn't, and I've not found the right one.

He calls it research.

I've thought about that word a great deal since you brought me his ledger, because I used to call what I did at the mill engineering, and the two things are closer than I'd like.

The difference is that I stopped when it killed somebody.

He did not. He initialled an order for more and dated it the same week.

So: it's murder. That's my word for it and I'll use it in front of him if I ever get the chance, which I won't, which is why I'm asking you.

The Alchemy Lab. Follow the smell.

And wear something you'd be happy to burn afterward. I mean that practically.
sps_at_helbrim.accept_text: The Alchemy Lab. Follow the smell.
sps_at_helbrim.turn_in_text:
It's over, then.

Not a clean ending. But a final one, and I've come round to thinking those are different things and I only get one of them.

Thank you.

sps_at_atiesh.description:
The tower's last occupant is Archmage Atiesh, and he keeps the Observatory.

Which is where the waygate was aimed.

I want to put those two facts next to each other because nobody at Ambermill has, and the moment you do, the whole building reorganises itself around them.

That tower isn't a tower with an observatory on top. It's an observatory with a tower under it, and everything beneath - the reading hall, the lab, the lecterns, Hawren - was support.

Somebody was looking at something for a very long time, and the waygate was how the looking got out.

I want to know what he was aiming at.

And I hope - I'll say this plainly and you can think what you like - I hope the answer dies with him.

The very top. The stair is long.

Don't stop on the landings. Not to rest, not to look. The landings are where it talks to you.
sps_at_atiesh.accept_text: The Observatory at the very top of the tower.
sps_at_atiesh.turn_in_text:
He aimed it at the stars.

Just the stars. That's all it was - a man looking up, for decades, carefully.

And then the stars aimed back.

Thank you. I'll be some time with that.

sps_at_orrery.description:
One last thing and then I'll lock the door.

The Orrery is the Observatory's twin. East of it - a round room full of little worlds, all still turning.

Still turning. Nobody has wound anything in that building for decades and those worlds are keeping time.

That's what the waygate has been feeding, as far as I can establish. Not the lamps, not the wards. The models.

And here's the thing I've worked out and cannot explain: they go out when somebody stands in the room.

A living person, present, for about a minute. Then the lamps settle and the little worlds slow, and when you leave they do not start again.

I don't know what that means. I know I want it done.

Observatory first. Then the Orrery to the east.

Stand a minute in each. That's all. Just be there.
sps_at_orrery.accept_text: The Observatory, then the Orrery east of it. Stand a minute in each.
sps_at_orrery.turn_in_text:
Dark. Both of them.

The waygate sleeps.

I'll lock it, and I'll keep the key somewhere stupid, and I'll not tell you where because then two of us would know.

sps_sfk_bailey.description:
Marl. Gatekeeper, which out here means I stand at a gate nobody goes through and nobody comes out of.

Nineteen years.

And in nineteen years I have never once met a person who could tell me what the forecourt looks like.

That's the thing that's finally broken me. People come out of Shadowfang - not many, but some, and I've spoken to every one of them. They'll tell you about the Great Hall. They'll tell you about the kennels at length.

Not one of them has ever described the bailey.

I've stopped thinking that's a coincidence and started thinking something in that courtyard doesn't get remembered.

So: through the portcullis, down the gatehouse passage, out into the bailey.

Stand by the fountain. It's dry - I know that much from the gate.

And then come back and tell me, while it's fresh.
sps_sfk_bailey.accept_text: Through the portcullis and the gatehouse passage, out to the bailey fountain.
sps_sfk_bailey.turn_in_text:
A dry fountain and a lot of bones.

I'd imagined worse. Nineteen years of imagining and it's bones.

You've got the nerve to go further. I'd like to make use of that.

sps_sfk_hounds.description:
Packbreaker Rynn. I'll be short - I don't like talking within sight of that gate.

I know the worgen on these hills. That's the trade and I'm good at it. I can tell you which hill a given worg runs, and roughly when, and what it's eating.

The ones in the keep are worse and they're worse in a specific way.

They're Arugal's own. Kennelled. Fed - deliberately, on a schedule, on things that used to be people.

A fed worg isn't a wolf anymore. A wolf hunts and fails and hunts again and that failure is what keeps it honest. These have never failed at anything.

Thin the kennels before I have to call them a pack.

That's not me being precious about words. A pack is a thing I know how to fight. What's in there hasn't got a leader yet - it's got a keeper - and the day those become the same thing, I'm out of trade.

The kennels, west of the bailey. They bark at nothing.

It isn't nothing.
sps_sfk_hounds.accept_text: The kennels, west of the bailey.
sps_sfk_hounds.turn_in_text:
A thinner pack.

Now it's a fight I can pick, instead of one that picks me.

That's the whole difference and nobody who isn't in this trade ever understands it.

sps_sfk_rethilgore.description:
Rethilgore keeps the hounds, and he keeps them hungry.

I want to be exact about that, because 'hungry' sounds like neglect and it isn't. It's a method. A fed hound sleeps. A hungry one watches the door.

He was a decent man in Pyrewood.

I didn't know him. I've been told by four people who did, and all four said the same word, which doesn't happen about a man unless it's true.

And I've watched him through a glass for a season, and the thing that unsettles me is that he's still careful. He checks the chains. He counts them.

So there's enough of him left to do the job properly, and not enough to stop doing it.

I'd like him buried before the keep makes him decent again - because I've seen that happen to one other and it was worse for everybody, him included.

The big pen in the west wing. He'll have a chain in his hand.
sps_sfk_rethilgore.accept_text: The kennels - the big pen in the west wing.
sps_sfk_rethilgore.turn_in_text:
He fed them first. Even then. You could see it.

I can respect that, I suppose.

I'd rather not have had to.

sps_sfk_razorclaw.description:
The Butcher's Yard is east of the bailey, and Razorclaw keeps it.

A worgen with a cleaver where a hand ought to be. Not holding one - instead of one, and I've had that confirmed by two people who got close enough to wish they hadn't.

I've heard the chopping from this gate for years.

That's the whole of my case and I know how thin it sounds in a report.

It's regular. That's what nobody understands when I say it. It isn't a frenzy and it isn't a fight - it's the sound of a man working, at a steady pace, for hours, and then stopping, and then starting again the next day.

Something is being prepared in that yard on a schedule, and the schedule has not changed in all the time I've stood here.

East of the bailey. Follow the sound.

You'll hear it from the gatehouse. Everyone does. Everyone decides it's something else.
sps_sfk_razorclaw.accept_text: The Butcher's Yard, east of the bailey. Follow the sound.
sps_sfk_razorclaw.turn_in_text:
The chopping's stopped.

Thank the Light.

I'll sleep tonight, for the first time in a long while, and I'll probably wake up listening for it.

sps_sfk_guards.description:
The keep's old guard never left their posts.

I'd call that loyalty if there were anybody left for them to be loyal to.

The guardsmen wail where they stood. Not where they fell - where they were POSTED, which I know because the positions make sense. Stand in the Great Hall and look at where they are and you can read the old watch order off them.

And the officers keep giving orders. To no one. Out loud, in the proper form, with pauses where the acknowledgement should go.

That's the part I can't get past, and it's why this is the job I'd most like done.

They were never relieved. Somebody should have come to take that watch and nobody ever did, and they are all still standing there waiting for it.

So relieve them. One way or another.

Officers first, then the men. That's the order it should have happened in and it's the only courtesy left to pay them.
sps_sfk_guards.accept_text: The Great Hall and the passages around it. Officers first.
sps_sfk_guards.turn_in_text:
Relieved. All of them.

It's a kindness, and I'm glad it wasn't me who had to do it, and I'm ashamed of being glad.

sps_sfk_keys.description:
A practical one, and it'll make everything after it cheaper.

The haunted servitors still carry the keep's keys on their belts.

Every one of them. A full ring each - and they're not guarding the doors, they're simply still carrying what they carried, because that's what a servitor does and nobody ever took them back.

Right now the cloisters and the armoury are a gamble.

That's the actual situation and it's cost people. You come to a door in that keep, you don't know if it's locked, and you find out by standing in front of it long enough for something to arrive.

I'd like the doors to stop being a gamble.

The Great Hall and the cloisters. Servitors carry a ring each.

Take the ring, not the key. I want whole rings - a ring tells you which doors went together, and that's a floor plan, and nobody's ever had one of those.
sps_sfk_keys.accept_text: Off the haunted servitors in the Great Hall and cloisters. Whole rings.
sps_sfk_keys.turn_in_text:
The right doors, and none of them haunted.

Almost enough to make a man hopeful.

Almost.

sps_sfk_silverlaine.description:
Baron Silverlaine owned Pyrewood, and Shadowfang, and half the pines between.

All of it. The road, the mill, the villages - every person who ever worked in this stretch of Silverpine worked it at his pleasure, and most of them never saw him.

He sits on his dais in the Great Hall and receives no one.

And that is exactly what he did alive. That's what's stayed with me since I worked it out - nothing about his conduct has changed. He held court, he received nobody, and he does the same now.

The only difference is that now there's genuinely nobody to receive.

I'd prefer the hall empty.

Not avenged. Not reckoned with. Empty - because as long as he's sitting at the far end of it, that keep still has an owner, and a keep with an owner is a place other things come to serve in.

The far end of the Great Hall.

He doesn't stand. He doesn't need to, and he never has.
sps_sfk_silverlaine.accept_text: The far end of the Great Hall, on the dais.
sps_sfk_silverlaine.turn_in_text:
A fitting end, I suppose.

He'd have called it a very modest funeral and he'd have meant it as a complaint.

sps_sfk_moonwalkers.description:
Arugal's cult is half sorcerers and half worgen who haven't decided yet.

That second half is what I want you looking at, because it's the thing nobody at the Rear Guard understands about this keep.

The moonwalkers are still turning. They're partway through it - and they chant, and the chanting is part of how they get the rest of the way.

The darksouls are what's at the end of that.

So it isn't a garrison with casters in it. The casters ARE the garrison - they're making more, continuously, out of whatever walks in.

The keep teems with them. I've counted from three different angles and stopped bothering, because the number isn't the point when the number is being manufactured.

Wherever you hear chanting.

Casters first. Always casters first, and I'd rather say it twice than find out you went in the other order.
sps_sfk_moonwalkers.accept_text: Throughout the keep, wherever you hear chanting. Casters first.
sps_sfk_moonwalkers.turn_in_text:
Fewer chants.

Perhaps the moon will go unremarked tonight, and that's the first time I've been able to say that in six years.

sps_sfk_cloister.description:
West of the Great Hall there's a stone cloister that runs out to Fenrus' crypt.

Nobody has walked it in years. I want to be careful there - not nobody has survived it. Nobody has WALKED it, because everyone who gets that far turns and takes the armoury stair instead, and when I ask them why they can't tell me.

I'd like it walked. Start to end.

And I'd like one specific thing from it, which is the only reason this is a job and not a curiosity.

I need to know whether the crypt door is open.

If it's shut, then whatever's in there has been shut in since Arugal's day and the keep has been containing it.

If it's open, then it has been open for years and everything in that building has been living alongside it on purpose.

Out of the west door of the Great Hall, down the cloister, into the crypt.

Just look. That's this job.
sps_sfk_cloister.accept_text: Out the west door of the Great Hall, down the cloister to the crypt.
sps_sfk_cloister.turn_in_text:
Open.

I'd hoped. I'd feared.

Both, honestly, and I'd not have been able to tell you which was stronger until you said it.

sps_sfk_fenrus.description:
Fenrus was Arugal's first experiment and his least successful.

I've had that from two sources and neither of them was being kind about it. Least successful means it didn't do what he wanted - not that it failed, because it is very much alive down there.

He devours things in the crypt.

And nothing that goes in comes out. That's not dramatic, it's a tally - I've kept the gate nineteen years and I know what's gone down that cloister, and I know what hasn't come back up it, and the two numbers are the same number.

I would like to be the exception.

That's my whole stake in this. I've stood at a gate nineteen years watching things go into a hole and I would like, once, for something to come back out of it on its own feet.

At the end of the cloister.

And mind the sarcophagi on the way down.

They breathe. I've been told that by three people and I've stopped asking them to explain it.
sps_sfk_fenrus.accept_text: The crypt at the end of the cloister. Mind the sarcophagi.
sps_sfk_fenrus.turn_in_text:
He ate his handler. And then his handler's replacement.

That's what least successful meant, and I've been chewing on it since you went down.

Thank you for being the exception.

sps_sfk_sons.description:
The inner keep is stocked with Arugal's best, and I use 'stocked' with intent.

Sons of Arugal in half-turned shapes. Lupine Horrors that do not fit through the doors they're standing behind - think about how one of those got into a room, and then stop thinking about it.

And Deathsworn Captains, who command them.

That last part is why I will not call this a pack, and I've had the argument with Marl twice.

A pack has an order of its own. It sorts itself out, it has a top and a bottom, and every animal in it knows where it stands without anybody writing it down.

This has officers.

Something decided who commands whom and told them, and that is a cult with fangs, not a pack - and the reason it matters is that a cult does not break when you kill the biggest one.

The crypt, the armoury and the upper landing.

Don't fight them in a corridor. That's where the Horrors are useful and they know it.
sps_sfk_sons.accept_text: The crypt, the armoury and the upper landing. Not in a corridor.
sps_sfk_sons.turn_in_text:
Not a pack. A cult, with fangs.

Fewer of those is a victory and I'll take it as one.

I'd still rather be fighting wolves.

sps_sfk_arugal.description:
Archmage Arugal opened the door that let the worgen into Lordaeron.

That's the sentence everybody knows and almost nobody follows through. He didn't summon a monster. He opened a DOOR, as a measure, against the Scourge - and it worked, briefly, and then it kept being open.

Everything in this valley since has come out of it. The hills, the keep, Pyrewood, Rynn's whole trade.

And he sits at the top of this keep with his tower of shadow, and as far as anyone can tell he thinks it went well.

I've stood at his gate nineteen years.

I'd like to see the other side of it. Not as a soldier - I'm not one, I'm a man with a halberd and a stool.

As somebody who has spent half his life being the last thing between that door and the road.

The upper landing, then the Sanctum.

Don't stop. And don't answer when he speaks - he will speak, and it will sound like a question you'd want to answer.
sps_sfk_arugal.accept_text: The upper landing, then Arugal's Sanctum at the top of the keep.
sps_sfk_arugal.turn_in_text:
Arugal. Dead.

I'll lock the gate and sit for a while. I'm going to sit for a long while.

Thank you. You'll never need to buy a drink at my post, and I'll be at it tomorrow, because I don't know how not to be.
